title: Sir Garry Sobers, Cricket's Greatest All-Rounder, Dies at 89 in Barbados
excerpt: The legendary West Indies captain held the record for highest Test score for 36 years, was the first to hit six sixes in an over, and was named a National Hero of Barbados.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Sir Garry Sobers, cricket's greatest all-rounder, died at 89 on July 17, 2026.
  • He scored 8,032 Test runs and took 235 wickets in 93 matches over 20 years.
  • Sobers held the highest Test score record for 36 years and hit six sixes in an over.
  • He was knighted by Queen Elizabeth II and named a National Hero of Barbados.
  • Sobers' legacy influences cricketers worldwide, especially in India.
  • Sir Garry Sobers, widely regarded as cricket's greatest all-rounder, died on July 17, 2026 at his home in Barbados at the age of 89
  • Over a 20-year career with the West Indies (1954–1974), Sobers scored 8,032 Test runs at an average of 57.78 and took 235 wickets across 93 matches
  • His 365 not out against Pakistan in 1958 stood as the highest individual Test score for 36 years, and he became the first cricketer to hit six sixes in a single over
  • Named a National Hero of Barbados, knighted by Queen Elizabeth II, and honored with the ICC's top men's player award bearing his name, Sobers leaves a legacy that transcends cricket

A Giant of the Game Falls Silent

Sir Garfield St Aubrun Sobers, the Barbadian cricketer who redefined what it meant to be an all-rounder, died on Friday at his home in Bridgetown, just 11 days short of his 90th birthday. Cricket West Indies confirmed the news with a simple tribute: "A great innings has come to an end. In our hearts, now and forever, Sir Garfield Sobers."

Born on July 28, 1936, as the fifth of six children, Sobers lost his father to the Second World War at the age of five. He made his first-class debut for Barbados at 16 and earned a West Indies Test cap a year later. What followed was a two-decade career that set the standard against which every cricketer since has been measured.

"Sir Garry's journey from Barbados to becoming the greatest cricketer the world has ever seen remains one of the most inspiring stories in the history of our game."

— Roston Chase, Hayley Matthews, and Shai Hope, West Indies Captains

"Cricket West Indies confirmed the news with a simple tribute: "A great innings has come to an end."

Records That Defined an Era

In 93 Tests for the West Indies, Sobers amassed 8,032 runs at an average of 57.78 — the fifth-highest among batters with more than 5,000 Test runs — and claimed 235 wickets at 34.03. He could bat anywhere in the order, bowl left-arm pace, orthodox spin, and wrist-spin, and was an exceptional close-in fielder. No cricketer before or since has combined such mastery across all three disciplines.

His 365 not out against Pakistan in Kingston in 1958, scored at the age of 21, set a world record for the highest individual Test innings. That mark stood for 36 years until his fellow Barbadian Brian Lara scored 375 against England in 1994. In 1968, playing for Nottinghamshire in the County Championship, Sobers became the first cricketer to strike six sixes in a single over, a feat that remains one of the sport's most celebrated moments.

Achievements highlighted in the article

Sobers captained the West Indies from 1965 to 1972, leading them in 39 Tests. In all first-class cricket, he scored over 28,000 runs and took more than 1,000 wickets across 383 matches.

Honours and Legacy

Queen Elizabeth II knighted Sobers in 1975 for his services to cricket. In 1998, an act of the Barbadian Parliament named him one of the country's 11 National Heroes. The International Cricket Council's most prestigious annual men's award, given to the world's best player across all formats, bears his name — the Sir Garfield Sobers Trophy.

Former West Indies captain Brian Lara, whose own record-breaking innings was inspired by Sobers, paid tribute: "Rest easy, legend. Your legacy will never be forgotten." Former England batsman Geoffrey Boycott described Sobers as a "once-in-a-lifetime" talent.

A Deep Connection to Indian Cricket

For the Indian cricket community worldwide, Sobers occupies a unique place. His West Indies teams of the 1960s and 1970s were the opponents that helped shape modern Indian cricket's identity, and his all-round brilliance set a benchmark that Indian greats from Kapil Dev to Ravindra Jadeja have been measured against. The ICC award bearing his name has been won by multiple Indian cricketers, including Virat Kohli and Sachin Tendulkar's contemporaries.

Legacy details from the article

Cricket West Indies CEO Chris Dehring said Sobers would "forever remain one of the greatest ambassadors" of the Caribbean. "His legacy will endure wherever cricket is played, and his spirit will live on every time a young West Indian dreams of wearing the maroon with distinction."

Sobers is survived by his family in Barbados. He will be remembered not only as a peerless cricketer but as a man who, despite National Hero status, remained deeply embedded in his community — known to cook lunch for workers at his home and chat with neighbors as if he were anyone else.
